chore(Pointer): add default target colours for pointer

As the shader is a transparent shader, the default colour when not
set is `Color.clear` which is also transparent which causes
confusion for users when using the script as the valid and invalid
target colours both have an alpha of zero.

This means that it's easy to set the colour of the target but forget
about setting the alpha so it seems as if the beams are broken but
in fact they are just completely transparent.

A simple solution is to just default the target colours with a
translucent colour so it's less confusing to new users.

feat(Pointer): add ability to provide custom game objects for beam

The Bezier Pointer now can have a custom game object provided for the
tracer beam instead of using the default sphere and a custom game
object can be provided for the cursor instead of using the default
cylinder.

fix(spelling): fix error with attach and detach

Attach and Detach were both spelt incorrectly.

chore(Interaction): consistent interaction buttons across examples

Previously, the example scenes had different button configurations for
interactions, some scenes used the Grip button for teleport and the
Trigger button for grab, where as other scenes used Touchpad for
teleport and the Grip button for grab.

This made it confusing to know what the buttons were per each scene.
They are now consistent across all examples with the following config:

  * `Touchpad Press` - Pointer
  * `Grip` - Grab
  * `Trigger` - User

feat(Pointer): add bezier curve pointer

The Bezier Pointer always shows a cursor on the top of any object and
draws a bezier curve to the ground cursor so it is easier to see where
the teleport location will end up.

A helper file has been added that takes care of calculating the bezier
curve and plotting a collection of spheres through it to simulate the
pointer beam over a curve. This bezier curve code is heavily inspired
by the code and tutorial at:
`http://catlikecoding.com/unity/tutorials/curves-and-splines/`

It is possible to set a valid beam colour and an invalid beam colour
which will determine if the beam has found a valid floor to land on.

A new example has been added to show the new Bezier Pointer working
with teleportation.

feat(Pointer): add play area cursor option to all pointers

The World Pointer abstract class now generates a play area cursor
that can be projected on to the end of any cursor that extends it.

The play area cursor can also handle collisions on the cursor end and
determine if the play area will be obstructed by other objects within
the cursor location. This can then be used to prevent teleporting
which will prevent players being in locations that they can clip into
objects.

The Simple Pointer and Bezier Pointer have been refactored so their
code that is the same between the two classes now sits in the World
Pointer class (as it's generic to all pointers). This provides the
two child pointers with more default parameters that are generic to
all child pointers as well.

The `Interfaces` directory has been renamed to `Abstractions` as the
World Pointer class isn't actually an interface so made no sense
calling the containing directory `Interfaces`.

A custom shader has been written to allow for Unlit Transparent colours
which work well with the pointers.

An example has been added that shows how the play area with collision
can be used to prevent players from teleporting to locations that would
mean they have the potential to walk into objects.

feat(Interaction): add example to show touchpad axis control

A new example has been added that contains an R/C car that is
controlled by moving a finger across the touchpad. Moving up and down
on the touchpad causese the car to drive forward and backward, moving
left and right causes the car to turn in that direction.

The trigger axis is also used to determine how high the car will jump
when the trigger is pressed.

feat(Pointer): add ability to provide custom game objects for beam

The Bezier Pointer now can have a custom game object provided for the
tracer beam instead of using the default sphere and a custom game
object can be provided for the cursor instead of using the default
cylinder.

feat(Teleport): add example of teleporting without using pointers

Now the Destination Events have been separated, it's possible to
trigger a teleport event via a means other than the world pointers.

The example scene shows how a model village of objects can be used
as map markers that determines where the user will be teleported to
upon touching and using one of the markers on the Play Area map.

Rescale the pointer in `VRTK_SimplePointer.Update()`, when the option to

fix(Pointer): ensure controller is valid before removing event handlers

The event handler removal in the OnDisable can cause a crash if the
controller object is no longer available. This fix ensures the event
handlers only get removed if the controller object is still valid.

chore(SDK): add support for a wider range of controller options

  > ** Breaking Changes **

The controller now supports an additional axis for the grip button
and the application menu button has been renamed to `Button One` as
other controllers may utilise this button for other purposes and a
generic name is more appropriate.

The grip and the button one can also register touch events in case
other controllers support touch on these input elements..

The SDK Manager has also been updated to now require the GameObjects
that contain the controller models to be supplied to the SDK Manager
so it can know where the renderers are for each controller and to
access the sub elements of the controller.

A button has been added to the SDK Manager custom inspector that when
clicked will attempt to find the linked objects automatically.

This will help in circumstances where the controller models are not
part of the actual tracked controller GameObject hierarchy.

The Controller Tooltips prefab has also been updated to reflect the
new Button One change.

feat(SDK): add simulator

Add new Simulator SDK for using mouse instead of controllers.
This will allow for using the mouse to move and rotate virtual
"hands" and allowing the developer to grab, use and in different
ways manipulating objects without the need of a VR controller.

perf(ControllerEvents): don't create garbage on vector comparison

Two `Vector2`s were compared by using a string based method which
creates garbage on every call which decreases performance. The solution
is to do it without using strings and only relying on stack allocated
structs.
Thanks to @reznovvr for this performance fix.

feat(Pointer): allow overriding of base pointer controller events

The pointer events by default all link to the AliasPointer events,
however it may be required to override those events with a custom
button press. It's now possible to override the button press and
have two pointers with different activation buttons by extending
a pointer script and overriding the `AliasRegistration` method.

In the future, there may be an inspector option to provide a button
override instead of needing to do it via script.

fix(Interaction): provide more natural door control

  > **Breaking Changes**

The 3D Door Control now uses the RotatorTrack grab mechanic to provide
a more natural door operation. The `Snapping` inspector parameter has
now been replaced with a float to determine the snap distance the door
has to be from being in a closed state before it snaps shut.

It is also possible now to provide the friction value that the door has
when it is being grabbed and moved, and the friction when it is not
being grabbed. A high grabbed friction gives a less bouncey feel and a
low ungrabbed friction allows the door to swing freely to allow for
slamming shut.

Another tweak is it is possible to apply the interactable object to the
entire door object rather than just the handle, which can be useful
for small doors such as cupboards, where it's desired to grab the door
to close it.

fix(Controls): use relative force to snap door shut

Relative force is more appropriate as it's relative the the door's
position and rotation, whereas using force will cause the door to
swing open in certain rotations.

Also, fixed an issue with a method with an incorrect case.

fix(UIPointer): clear existing pointer enter on invalid hover

There was an issue where if a UI button click would disable the canvas
and enable another canvas, then the previous pointer enter selection
would not be cleared and therefore if a button on the new canvas was
selected, it would not have the UI events passed to it as they would
still be tied to the old pointer entry.

This fix ensures the pointer enter event data is cleared up correctly.

Thanks to @nvisionGeo for reporting the issue and posting the fix.

fix(UI): allow non-VR UI usage

This fix makes it possible to use Unity UI in the regular, non-VR way
while making sure the VR UI interactions provided by VRTK still work.

Since this introduces a new class `VRTK_EventSystem` the existing logic
to disable the auto-pausing behavior in Unity 5.5 and above is moved
into the new class. Possible confusion regarding the naming of the
existing `VRTK_EventSystemVRInput` and the new class is resolved by
changing the name of the existing class to `VRTK_VRInputModule`. An
unused constant of `VRTK_UIPointer` is also removed.

fix(Pointer): ensure enum comments match actual enum names

The Pointer Visibility enums don't have underscores in the name but
the xml documentation contained underscores.

This has been fixed and the documentation updated.

fix(Highlighters): explicitly check for null arrays in outline

The outline object copy highlighter could still throw a null
reference exception even though the arrays should be instantiated.

This additional check makes sure they're not null before dealing
with them.

feat(Pointer): add method to reset pointer objects at runtime

The pointer cursor and pointer tracer are created in the OnEnable
method which means if a custom tracer/cursor are provided at runtime
then they cannot be switched without disabling and re-enabling the
pointer script.

A new method has been added that can be called which simply destroys
the existing pointer objects and recreates them, so any custom
changes will be present in the update. This also happens without
affecting the existing state of the pointer.

chore(THANK_YOU_CREDITS.md): add name to list

Roland has now been added to the list as well.

fix(Pointer): prevent null exception when pointer has no renderer

The Pointer Renderer script would throw an exception if it hadn't
been assigned to a Pointer due to the smoothing object trying to
be updated but not having a controller pointer.

This fix ensures the controlling pointer is set to prevent the
null exception.

fix(Pointer): reduce BEAM_ADJUST_OFFSET distance in renderer

The `BEAM_ADJUST_OFFSET` in the base pointer renderer is used to adjust
any ray position back slightly to prevent it from clipping when cast.

However, having such a low offset can cause issues in edge cases like
if the terrain is set at a Y above 255 then the offset isn't enough and
the ray will cast straight through the floor.

feat(Structure): add standard method for naming generated objects

Any VRTK generated GameObject now goes through a standard method in
VRTK_SharedMethods that standardises the GameObject names so they are
all easily identified as VRTK required objects.

fix(Pointer): reset destination hit info on activate

The `destinationHit` variable was not being reset after the pointer
was disabled, meaning if the pointer was deactivated over a valid
object and then reactivated over that same object then the
`PointerEnter` method would not call the `OnDestinationMarkerEnter`
event.

The fix ensures the `destinationHit` is cleared whenever the
pointer is toggled on so it has a fresh state.

feat(Pointer): move direction indicator into base renderer

The Pointer Direction Indicator parameter is now on the Pointer
Renderer rather than the top level pointer. This means that different
renderers can contain different pointer supplements and be swapped
out at runtime.

fix(Pointer): provide default boundary data if none available

If the PlayAreaCursor script is dealing with an SDK that has no
available boundary data it would cause a crash when attempting
to access the Vector3 array.

This fix provides a default array to prevent a crash.

feat(Interaction): add near touch to interact haptics

The Interact Haptics script has also been refactored to use the

script.

and unsubscribe from these interaction events and the Interact
Object Highlighter has also been refactored to use these new event
subscription helpers.

feat(Pointers): match play area cursor rotation to direction indicator

The Play Area Cursor script can now accept a Pointer Direction
Indicator which if provided will be used to amend the rotation of the

If no Pointer Direction Indicator is provided then the rotation will

fix(UI): prevent crash when no pointer is attached to UI Pointer

There was an issue where the VRInputModule would crash if no controller
was attached to the UI Pointer because it was trying to access a

feat(Interaction): add physics pusher controllable

fix(Pointers): ensure pointer id exists when checking ui pointer length

length from the dictionary and making the dictionary protected whilst

fix(Pointers): handle destroyed origin transform follow

fix(Examples): remove script define symbol check and provide popup

open the example constructor scene before opening any of the example
scenes did not work if no 3rd party SDK was installed that required
it. It would simply just continually throw the error message.

The new solution is not to try and second guess what the set up is
automatically and to just provide a popup window with information
for the user on requiring them to open the constructor example scene.

fix(settings): provide additional default project settings

Unity in all it's wisdom, seems to store the lock input to game view
settings within the Library directory rather than the ProjectSettings
directory, meaning that any new check out of the project doesn't have
the input locked to the game view which then throws an error in Unity
because it expects the input to be locked when in VR.

settings file and then when a new project is opened, the remaining

feat(Operation): ability to extract the position data from a Transform

GameObject.

feat(Interactions): nest common prefab functionality in interactors

The interactor prefab has now been updated to break the internal
functionality up into appropriate nested prefabs so both the Touch
logic as well as the Grab logic now come via their own prefabs.

chore(structure): use serialized properties via Malimbe

Instead of writing a property and a backing field manually Malimbe
allows to just annotate the property with an attribute to ensure the
backing field is serialized. Besides that change the usages of the
updated members also have been updated and methods were added that
ensure changes to the property are handled in a boilerplate-free
way. This includes moving the property logic into "OnChange" methods
with the help of Malimbe to prevent having to write the property and
backing field combination if all that's needed is customizing the
getter or setter.

feat(Process): randomize the start time for interval running

While the interval setting on processes allows to improve
performance by doing work less often, there was still an issue in
case many processes were running at the same time. This was
primarily happening for objects already in the scene at startup of
the play session. Instead of saving performance by running processes
less often one could now have performance issues due to "spikes" as
multiple processes all ran at the same time. This change improves on
the interval behavior by introducing a randomization to the
calculation of the target time of a process. Once the first process
call has been done it won't be randomized any further automatically,
but users are able to call the same randomization logic in form of a
newly added method when needed.

feat(Type): add collapsible UnityEvent drawer

A new custom PropertyDrawer that overrides the UnityEventDrawer has
been added to allow the ability to wrap a UnityEvent inspector control
in a foldout so the UnityEvent control can be collapsed.

Reflection is required to override the default UnityEventDrawer
inspector drawing ue to the way Unity creates the UnityEventDrawer
internally.

feat(Rule): add rule to check if a string pattern is in a string list

The StringInListRule allows a string pattern to be specified to match
against any string found in an associated String Observable List that
is a component on the given GameObject.

This can replace the need to use the AnyComponentTypeRule and creating
dummy scripts for tags as the string list can be used as the tag name
that is then picked up by the rule.

feat(Extraction): add extractors for ObjectFollower.EventData

A collection of extractors that can extract specific data from
the ObjectFollower.EventData.

For example, an Interactable is using Follow Rigidbody.
When it is diverged, the event data can be feed into the
ObjectFollowerEventDataSourceExtractor to get the grabbing
interactor.

feat(Type): add ability to provide easy reference access to Objects

The new ObjectReference type and custom drawer allow a Object
to be specified as a property which can then be shown as a simple
button in the inspector to highlight the referenced Object within
the Unity Hierarchy.

script.

feat(Pointers): match play area cursor rotation to direction indicator

The Play Area Cursor script can now accept a Pointer Direction
Indicator which if provided will be used to amend the rotation of the
Play Area Cursor to match the Pointer Direction Indicator.

If no Pointer Direction Indicator is provided then the rotation will
simply match the Playarea rotation.

fix(Pointers): turn off renderer when either script is disabled

There was an issue where if the Pointer was active in the scene but
either the Pointer script or the Pointer Renderer script were disabled
then the Pointer Renderer would stay visible on the screen.

This fix ensures that when the Pointer script is disabled it
automatically calls `Toggle(false)` to turn off the pointer and also
checks the state of the attached Pointer Renderer and if it is disabled
the `Toggle(false)` is also called to ensure the pointer is disabled.

fix(UI): prevent crash when no pointer is attached to UI Pointer

There was an issue where the VRInputModule would crash if no controller
was attached to the UI Pointer because it was trying to access a
controller to get the touchpad axis data for the scroll amount.

This has been fixed by checking for the existence of a controller.

feat(Interaction): add physics pusher controllable

The Physics Pusher controllable creates a joint object that can have
physics force applied to move the controllable in a designated
direction to simulate a button.

deprecating all of the existing 3D controls as they are being replaced

a parameter to perform additional permissions tests based on where it's
called from (often for Modify permission but sometimes Copy or Trans).

in some cases for linking and unlinking, removing from contents, deeding
objects to group, Undo and Redo, changing prim or object scale, changing
prim/object name, description, flags, textures, and materials.  Also did
some cleanup (TestPermissionBasics was only a SOG find function that
ignored most parameters), but did not return the SOG found, which leaves
race conditions and failure conditions for the caller.  Now it returns a
reference to the SOG in one atomic Try operation.  Note: In some cases,
redundant existing perms checks remain in place. These can be removed
eventually but were not done in this commit to minimize visual changes.

  base class, and move it to the specific NodeDssSignaler
  implementation.

Note that currently Signaler encapsulates messages into a Message type,
which is then re-encapsulated into a different NodeDssMessage type by
the NodeDssSignaler. This looks redundant, but there are 2 reasons for
this:
- NodeDssSignaler needs a specific message type that serializes to JSON

  protocol.

Fix Shader import error seen on Mac editor

OnLoadUtilities.cs fails to copy shaders when running on MacOS due to
a filename sensitivity issue.

The constant `ShaderSentinelFile = "MRTK.Shaders.Sentinel";` refers to
a file that is actually named `MRTK.Shaders.sentinel` with a lowercase
`s` on sentinel.

On MacOS DirectoryInfo.GetFiles appears to be case-sensitive even if
the underlying filesystem is not. This causes the script to not find
MRTK.Shaders.sentinel and thus not be able to copy the shaders.

Fix the issue by using a lowercase `s` in the constant.
